checks: Read the source records at the declared raw hashes. In 1a7cfa3d1047cbae §§5–6 (14)–(18) give the allocated density, force, tensor and actual affine transport. In 8f0725a173821a00 §§4–5 (18)–(23) give the regular singleton case. In 7127f9c7b67df7cb §4 (9) gives the supporting-cap formula with unit normals; the revised reference now points to that exact equation.

At h=ν=0 the mass-unit coefficient −βD and each e_ia times the contact bracket give Xi exactly, including −k log L from −s(v)/N. The sign of the cap sectional flux is positive because the proper truncated body has new cut normal −u/||u||. On an inside face keep the full boundary flux and zero section; on an outside face its outward normal is +u/||u|| and the common selector cancels it with the zero-volume sectional term. Strict full/empty and fixed pure-base caps have whole-fiber/zero flux. The same rules hold by the endpoint formula in dimension one.

Divergence of the projective kernel gives −N a_a P_a^(−N−1), hence its e_ia-weighted force is −e_ia a_a and its tensor is e_ia I_d/N−e_ia y_ia⊗a_a. The centered quadratic has zero force by the definition of g_z. The positive finite-plane L is Lipschitz on the needed neighborhood and its log has weak derivative c/L almost everywhere, so the force and tensor use the volume derivative directly.

For a positive group the cap force is κ_i U_i and its base moment is ∑_a κ_ia p_ia⊗U_i; use the full weighted section mean and the zero base component of the covariance shift. The contact identity and labeled tilted first moments cancel the energy and logarithmic terms, with Δ/(NM) obtained by dividing the labeled coefficient Δ/M by N.

The cap tensor has raw QI_d after summing all proper and atomic weights, canceling −βMI_d. Its section contribution is ∑_ia κ_ia y_ia⊗U_i−∑_i e_i Σ C_i^u. The covariance quadratic gives Δ I_d/2 using uᵀΣu=1 and derivative term ∑_i e_i Σ C_i^u using ∫X⊗(X−g_z)=∫(X−g_z)⊗(X−g_z) on each fiber. The energy, quadratic and constant scalar coefficients are Δ[1/N+1/2−(N+2)/(2N)]=0. The log scalar term vanishes by ∫log L=0; its remaining tensor cancels via the continuous-position label moment and the contact identity. Trace then yields the radial expression, and an affine g_z pairs to zero with the total and base force sums.

Under an invertible lattice-preserving fiber-affine map, every volume and marked energy gain |det A|, Σ transforms to AΣAᵀ, the continuous normal becomes A^(−ᵀ)u and transported L has unchanged mean log. Cap ratios and buffered margins are therefore preserved exactly. For a smooth base-fixed action the old plane margin derivative is −u·V. At inside and outside faces the respective oriented hinge quantities (r−ν·w)/||u||−v and (ν·w−r)/||u||−v vanish using v=−n·V; no raw derivative across a moving crease is needed.

overlap.comparison: The body-tied construction supplies common allocated cap loads and affine balance on its own stress density. The body-tied term e_ia/(dNV_z) and its total-mass coefficient differ from this density’s full-space continuous log term. It does not give the stated formula for the same log-parameter separator or the labeled volume cancellations.

Its invariance of normalized cap masses under lattice-preserving fiber-affine maps uses the same determinant and normal-covariance transformations with the tied profile. The present extension pulls back the independent full-space log parameter and checks the supporting hinges along actual transported paths.
Its moving-shell formula supplies the two signed supporting hinges that vanish on transported cap/body actions, without the common density or affine moment identities.
